title: Traffic contingency decision graph prototype
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Design and prototype a decision-graph UI inside Redwood Console that helps engineers and SREs choose safe, cost-aware traffic contingency actions during staged rollouts. The graph combines live telemetry signals (error rate, latency, token-cost delta, infra saturation) with rollout configuration (variants, audience slices, weights) to surface recommended mitigation actions: pause, partial rollback, targeted quarantine of cohorts, shadow traffic, or scope down model variant. Deliver a clickable prototype that maps signal thresholds to suggested actions and shows estimated cost and latency impact for each action.
acceptance_criteria: Interactive graph prototype in Figma showing node types: signal, decision, mitigation, and action
Telemetry mapping panel that links to Console metrics dashboards for each signal
Cost delta preview for each mitigation option (rough token-cost estimate)
Fallback quick-actions that create a console operation (e.g., pause rollout, set traffic to 0% for a variant) with clear consequence text
Design documentation describing UX rules for automated vs manual suggestions and thresholds
Sign-off from PM and at least one backend engineer verifying feasibility of quick-action payloads
comments: 2026-02-20 — Sofia: Kickoff session with PM and runtime lead. Agreed primary signals: 5xx rate, p95 latency, token cost delta, queue depth. Decided scope for first iteration: single-rollout view and cohort quarantine action.
2026-02-27 — Amelia: Wireframes added to Figma. Two interaction patterns explored: timeline-first and graph-first. UX review favored graph-first for incident triage flows.
2026-03-02 — Ravi Menon (Eng): Backend can expose aggregate token-cost delta per variant via /rollouts/:id/metrics. Need a small API change; ENG dependency noted.
2026-03-04 — Usability test (4 participants): Ops users found quick-action confirmation copy ambiguous. Updated copy to include 'expected user-visible effects' and 'estimated cost impact'.
2026-03-08 — PM review (Liam Chen): Request to surface 'confidence' for automated suggestions and to include a 'why this action' explain panel linked to recent incidents. Added as next-step.

2026-03-10 — Design review with Security: Confirmed quick-actions require RBAC check and audit log entry. Security flagged requirement to show the principal who approved automatic fallback; added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-12 — Amelia: Prototype ready for engineering feasibility check. Linked PR and backend spike. Next: sync with runtime for KV cache considerations when quarantining cohorts.
notes: This design intentionally emphasizes explainability: each suggested mitigation must include which signal crossed threshold and an example of user-visible effect.
Cost previews are rough estimates derived from recent token consumption patterns and should be surfaced with a confidence band.
We will instrument a lightweight A/B test in the console (opt-in for customers) to compare decision-graph-assisted rollouts vs manual rollouts for MTTR and number of rollbacks.
